sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: System design questions for Rails engineers combine general distributed systems knowledge with Rails-specific implementation patterns. Caching in Rails has multiple layers — HTTP caching with ETags, fragment caching, Russian doll caching, and the Rails cache store (usually Redis). Scaling Rails means understanding Puma thread count, database connection pool sizing, read replicas with ActiveRecord::Base.connected_to, and horizontal scaling with stateless servers. Multi-tenancy is a recurring architecture question at SaaS Rails companies — row-level isolation with a tenant scope, schema-per-tenant with the Apartment gem, or database-per-tenant each with different trade-offs. This page covers each with concrete Rails examples and the capacity numbers interviewers expect.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: caching-strategies, scaling-rails-patterns, rate-limiting-design, multi-tenancy. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
